newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African pharmacy plan raises industry hackles.
newsitem.headline: S.African pharmacy plan raises industry hackles.

text.p: South Africa's pharmaceutical industry on Monday warned that government plans to allow non-pharmacists to open and run pharmacies would make control of medicines difficult.
The moves are part of Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma's efforts to ensure easy access to cheaper medicines.
"This opens up a can of worms in that the control of medicines will become almost totally impossible," said Naseem Kamdar, executive member of the Family Practitioners' Association.
Representatives from a wide range of professional bodies were making their case to the parliamentary portfolio committee on health during a public hearing on the Pharmacy Amendment Bill.
Other industry groups included the South African Pharmacy Council, the United South African Pharmacies, and the South African Association of Hospital and Institutional Pharmacists.

Zuma's other plans to allow for the wider prescription of cheaper generic drugs have already upset the pharmaceuticals industry, with some United States firms threatening not to invest in South Africa until Zuma changes her mind.

Pharmacists said that allowing non-pharmacists to operate pharmacies would open the way for large companies and chainstores to run pharmacies for profit and not with the best interests of the public in mind.

But some delegates said they were confused by the late submission of amendments to the bill on Monday and said that they could not comment meaningfully on it until they were given full new copies of the bill.
The amendments were discussed with Zuma by the Interim Pharmacy Council of South Africa on June 3 but had not been passed on to other organisations before the hearing.
